According to him, the initiative formed part of his plan to move the economy away from dependence on public revenue distribution towards productive activities capable of generating wealth and employment. He also questioned the Federal Government’s continued borrowing despite claims of improved revenue collection and substantial external reserves, arguing that economic management should translate into tangible benefits for businesses and ordinary Nigerians. The APM candidate urged voters in the South-East to support his presidential ambition, acknowledging the region’s political importance and promising to take his campaign message to every part of the country. Earlier, the APM national chairman criticised the state of the economy and called on President Bola Tinubu to support Makinde’s presidential ambition. “Every Nigerian is aware that this country has not had it this bad. The chairman questioned why Nigerians were not benefiting sufficiently from increases in international petroleum prices, given the country’s status as an oil-producing nation. He also expressed concern over the country’s security challenges. Recalling Makinde’s support for Tinubu through the G5 governors during the 2023 presidential election, the chairman urged the President to reciprocate the gesture. “Last time, you supported the president through the G5 governors. Now it is your turn, and the president should support you. I am calling on President Bola Tinubu to step down and support Seyi Makinde,” he said. The Director-General of the campaign, Felix Hyat, also appealed to South-East residents to support Makinde, citing his policy proposals and leadership experience. Hyat lamented the economic difficulties facing households, saying many Nigerians were struggling to meet their family needs. “It is unfortunate that our people can no longer cope with family demands because of the bad economy. It is time for the young people to vote them out,” he said. He also commended Makinde’s choice of a security expert as his running mate, describing the ticket as capable of addressing the country’s challenges. item.title: 154 students hospitalised over suspected drug reaction in Katsina
item.description: One hundred and fifty-four students of Government Science Secondary School, Batagarawa, Katsina State, were hospitalised following a suspected adverse reaction to praziquantel tablets administered to treat bilharzia. The incident occurred on Monday, according to a statement issued on Wednesday by the Katsina State Police Command’s Public Relations Officer, Abubakar Sadiq Aliyu. Aliyu said the students reportedly developed symptoms of an adverse drug reaction after receiving the tablets from the school authorities. Praziquantel is used to treat schistosomiasis, also known as bilharzia, a parasitic disease associated with contact with freshwater contaminated by the parasites. The police spokesman said the affected students were taken to hospital for treatment, with no casualties or deaths recorded. He added that the remaining 25 students, who had been kept in hospital for further medical attention, had also been treated and discharged. According to him, all the affected students were in good health and had been reunited with their families and schoolmates. The Commissioner of Police, Ali Umar Fage, thanked members of the public for their cooperation and calmness during the incident. He urged residents to refrain from spreading unverified reports and rumours, assuring them that the command would continue to protect lives and property across the state. item.title: INEC moves to tackle electoral risks in Abia
item.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has stepped up preparations for the 2027 general elections, with efforts to identify and address potential threats to peaceful and credible polls in Abia State. The Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in the state, Prof. Sylvia Agu, disclosed this on Thursday in Umuahia at a stakeholder sensitisation workshop on Electoral Risk Management (ERM). Agu said early identification of electoral threats, effective coordination and collaboration among stakeholders were critical to preventing disruptions and strengthening public confidence in the electoral process. “Successful elections require deliberate preparation, effective coordination and the collective commitment of all institutions and individuals involved in the electoral process,” she said. She urged stakeholders, particularly security agencies, to sustain their cooperation with INEC to ensure peaceful elections and strengthen democracy. The Abia State Commissioner of Police, CP Wilfred Olutokunbo Afolabi, also reaffirmed the police commitment to credible elections. Represented by the Deputy Commissioner of Police in charge of Operations, DCP Ifeanyi Uzor, Afolabi said the police would protect election materials, provide security for National Youth Service Corps members and ensure a safe environment for voters. “The 2027 election will not be an exception. We have a renewed commitment from the Inspector-General of Police to ensure credible elections in 2027. That duty we must perform without fear or prejudice,” he said. Also speaking, the INEC Administrative Secretary in Abia, Chief Ama Agwu, said the ERM framework would help identify, assess and manage security threats, political tensions, environmental challenges and operational difficulties capable of disrupting elections. Agwu urged electoral officers to ensure that information gathered was accurate, verified and reflective of conditions on the ground to facilitate timely interventions. Earlier, the Head of the Department of Planning and Monitoring, Mr Ogbuisi Robinson, said the workshop was designed to identify electoral risks specific to Abia, strengthen early-warning and response mechanisms, and promote evidence-based planning. He said the exercise would also involve collaboration with the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES). INEC officials, including Electoral Officers from all 17 local government areas in Abia, representatives of security agencies and other stakeholders attended the workshop. The ICPC alleged that the defendant, while passing himself off as a public servant, obtained over N27 billion to start the fake agency. item.title: Trump says Brazil election was ‘a disgrace’
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Thursday stepped up criticism of Brazil’s “disgraceful” election, declining to say whether he recognized leftist Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva as president after right-wing rival Flavio Bolsonaro claimed victory. “I think the election was a disgrace in Brazil,” Trump told reporters when asked if he accepted Lula’s victory, a day after his ally Bolsonaro fled to the United States and proclaimed himself the rightful leader. “I don’t want to comment on it right now, but I thought the election was a very great embarrassment to the people of Brazil… I thought it was a very disgraceful situation for Brazil.” The post Trump says Brazil election was ‘a disgrace’ appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Digital divide could become new colonialism — Russia warns
item.description: … Offers AI research partnership to Africa By Nkiruka Nnorom Russia has warned that unregulated development of Artificial Intelligence, AI, risks deepening global inequality and creating a new form of colonialism, with Africa at risk of becoming a raw-material appendage of the AI economy. The warning was issued by Andrey Akulchev, Acting Director of Department of International Information Security of Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, at the session “AI as a Factor in Development of Russia and Africa: Science and Personnel” held as part of business programme of third Russia-Africa Economic and Humanitarian Forum in Moscow. “If development of artificial intelligence is left unregulated, digital divide could become a new global watershed and fertile ground for modern forms of colonialism,” Akulchev said. According to him, Russia advocates equal access to technology and takes the interests of countries of Global South into account. “Africa must not become either a raw-material appendage of the new AI-based economy or a free data warehouse for those who train their models on it,” he stated. Akulchev disclosed that within framework of Russia-Africa summit, a separate declaration on AI has been agreed, which enshrines right of each country to independently determine its policy in this area and supports multilingual solutions, including Swahili, Yoruba, Hausa, Amharic and Zulu. Also speaking at same session, First Deputy Minister of Economic Development of Russian Federation, Maxim Kolesnikov, said Russia has been supporting 13 research centres in the field of artificial intelligence, where more than 2,000 scientists work since 2021. He said the centres are open to cooperation with African colleagues. “We also invite our African colleagues to cooperate on basis of our laboratories. Together with foreign scientists from our centres, as well as foreign partner centres from 36 countries, we held International AI Foresight last year,” Kolesnikov said. He noted that one of the preparatory sessions of the foresight was held in Morocco with participation of representatives of African countries. Both interventions formed part of broader push by Moscow to position AI cooperation as pillar of Russia-Africa partnership, anchored on technological sovereignty, local capacity building and respect for national regulatory autonomy, rather than one-way technology transfer. It is very worrisome and very disturbing,” Agbedi said. He recalled raising similar concerns in 2016, warning that the life of a Nigerian appeared to be worth only a minute of silence in the face of persistent attacks. While acknowledging the efforts of security personnel, Agbedi questioned whether the country was doing enough to protect citizens, calling for technology-driven operations capable of identifying attackers and tracking their movements. “That assailants will come, miscreants will come, terrorists will come, kidnappers will come and carry out these mind-blowing acts and there will be no trace to it is worrisome,” he said. According to him, more than 124,000 fighters and their family members had surrendered since 2023, while over 104 communities had been brought under safe corridors through legislative interventions and security operations involving the Multinational Joint Task Force. The Deputy Speaker also said the number of local government areas under insurgent control had declined from 17 in 2022 to six, based on information available to the House in 2025. He added that security spending rose from ₦2.98 trillion in 2023 to ₦3.25 trillion in 2024, ₦4.291 trillion in 2025 and ₦5.4 trillion in 2026. The Deputy Speaker said the figures demonstrated that the government was acting on resolutions passed by the legislature, adding that the minute of silence was intended to honour the victims and was not the House’s only response to insecurity. item.title: Edo Queens miss CAF Women’s Champions League after controversial WAFU-B final replay
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Nigeria Women’s Football League (NWFL) champions, Edo Queens, have lost their place in the 2026 CAF Women’s Champions League after suffering a 3-2 defeat to Ghana’s Ampem Darkoa Ladies in a controversial replay of the WAFU-B qualifying final in Cairo, Egypt, on Thursday. Mohammed Afishata scored in the 92nd minute to hand Ampem Darkoa victory after the match resumed from the beginning of extra time, following a ruling by the Confederation of African Football (CAF). Edo Queens had initially won the September 5 final in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso, after the match ended 2-2 in regulation time and they triumphed in the ensuing penalty shootout. However, CAF later nullified the result after ruling that the match officials had wrongly proceeded directly to penalties without playing the mandatory 30 minutes of extra time. Following an appeal by Ampem Darkoa, CAF ordered that the omitted extra time be played, with the score restored to 2-2. The replay took place in Cairo on Thursday, with Ampem Darkoa taking advantage of the opportunity to score early in extra time and secure a 3-2 victory, ending Edo Queens’ hopes of qualifying for the continental competition. Edo Queens made two changes to their team for the resumed match, bringing in Kafayat Mafisere and Mary Mamudu for Oluwakemi Adegbuyi and Oluebube Umejiaku, who were away on national duty. The Nigerian champions, however, failed to find a late equaliser as the Ghanaian side held on to secure qualification. The victory gives Ampem Darkoa their second appearance at the CAF Women’s Champions League, having last featured in the competition in 2023 in Côte d’Ivoire. The Ghanaian club will compete in Group B alongside defending champions AS FAR of Morocco, USFAS Bamako of Mali and Kawempe Muslim Ladies of Uganda. Edo Queens, who reached the semi-finals on their debut in 2024, will miss this year’s tournament following the defeat. The 2026 CAF Women’s Champions League is scheduled to hold in Egypt from November 1 to 15. item.title: Carrick not surprised he’s still Man Utd manager
item.description: Under-pressure Manchester United manager Michael Carrick said Thursday he was “here to do my job” as he insisted he needed “no assurances” over his future at Old Trafford. Carrick also said he was unsurprised to still be in charge after a woeful run of results and gave his backing to United captain Bruno Fernandes. Portugal midfielder Fernandes was left on the bench for last week’s loss at home to Bournemouth following his criticism of Carrick’s tactics in a 4-1 thrashing by Como. Carrick’s position has been the subject of intense speculation after a miserable run of eight games without a win. Sunday’s 3-0 humbling loss at home to Bournemouth left the English giants one point above the Premier League relegation zone. United have won just two of 12 matches in all competitions this season, with a return of seven points from eight league games representing their worst start to a league season in 40 years. But Carrick remains in charge and, speaking ahead of Saturday’s match away to Chelsea, the 45-year-old former United and England midfielder was in defiant mood. Asked if he was still surprised to be in post, he told reporters: “No. I’m here to do my job. I’m here to do the best for the team. I’m desperate to make things better and improve things. I’m not surprised, no.” – ‘Get the position’ – Carrick was equally adamant he did not require public backing from the United hierarchy. “I don’t need assurances from anyone,” he said. “I totally get the position, I get the job, the responsibility, I get what comes with that.” Questioned on Fernandes’s position, Carrick said leaving him on the bench against Bournemouth was a “decision for the game”. “That’s it. Bruno is fully committed to this football club. I’ve got no issues with that, we move forward. We’re looking forward to the game at the weekend now.” Carrick appears to have the backing of the United faithful, being warmly applauded by fans as he made his way down the tunnel following the defeat by Bournemouth. Moments later a chorus of boos erupted as the players left the pitch as supporters made clear where they think the blame lies for United’s poor performances. Nevertheless, former United captain Gary Neville, who played alongside Carrick at Old Trafford said earlier Thursday that “sometimes a manager needs sacking for their own good”. But Carrick was adamant he would not walk away from his job. “I genuinely don’t take any notice of anything else. I know this job and I know what we need to be better. I don’t need anyone else to tell me…I’ve said it before, I care about what the supporters think…I care about what we give them and what they see.” And he insisted his much criticised players cared, too. “The boys are hungry,” he said. “We’re hurting because we haven’t won enough football games. But there is an intensity, an edge, a hunger to do better.” AFP The post Carrick not surprised he’s still Man Utd manager appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: PANDEF demands 50% oil derivation for Niger Delta
item.description: By Daniel Abia PORT HARCOURT — The Pan Niger Delta Elders Forum (PANDEF) has called on the Federal Government to increase the derivation allocation to oil-producing states from the current minimum of 13 per cent to 50 per cent, citing environmental degradation and the developmental challenges facing the region. The group also urged the government to invest in modular refineries to complement existing refining facilities, while insisting that the completion of the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway and East-West Road projects must not be compromised. The demands were contained in a 48-point communiqué jointly signed by former Akwa Ibom State Governor, Obong Victor Attah, Chairman of PANDEF’s Board of Trustees, and its National Chairman, Dr. Godknows Boladei Igali. The communiqué followed a virtual meeting of the Board of Trustees and National Executive Committee of the forum on Tuesday. PANDEF noted that Section 162(2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, provides for the allocation of not less than 13 per cent of revenue accruing directly from natural resources to states from which the resources are derived. It also established a high-level technical committee to assist the Federal Ministry of Works on the project, which it said had been under consideration since before Nigeria’s independence. PANDEF further called for the completion of the East-West Road and urged the Federal Government to establish appropriate north-south rail connections to link the Niger Delta with other parts of the country. The forum also commended President Bola Tinubu’s decision to modernise and upgrade the ports in Warri, Port Harcourt and Calabar. It welcomed approvals for proposed deep seaports, including the Ibom Deep Sea Port in Akwa Ibom State, Bonny Deep Sea Port in Rivers State and Agge Deep Sea Port in Bayelsa State. According to PANDEF, the strategic location of the proposed ports could strengthen trade links with East, Central and Southern Africa and improve access to international shipping routes. PANDEF seeks investment in modular refineries The forum called for greater investment in agriculture as a central pillar of the Niger Delta’s economic diversification strategy, arguing that the region’s natural resources should be harnessed to create sustainable prosperity and economic value. It also urged the government to support modular refineries to complement large-scale facilities, including the Dangote Refinery and the Port Harcourt, Warri and Kaduna refineries, alongside other private-sector refining projects. PANDEF said a properly regulated modular refining industry could reduce dependence on imported petroleum products, support local businesses, create jobs and stimulate related industries across the Niger Delta and the wider Nigerian economy. The forum said coordinated investment in infrastructure, environmental restoration, refining and agriculture was necessary to address the region’s longstanding challenges and expand economic opportunities for its people. item.title: 2027: Makinde targets jobs, manufacturing in APM agenda
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike The Oyo State Governor and presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has promised to prioritise job creation, skills training and manufacturing as part of his party’s agenda for Nigeria, with its manifesto scheduled for unveiling on November 4. Makinde spoke at the APM South-East town hall meeting in Enugu, where he said the party had consulted Nigerians across the six geopolitical zones to develop solutions to unemployment, poverty, insecurity and the trust deficit between leaders and citizens. Makinde said the party’s agenda rested on four pillars: economic recovery, security restructuring, education reform and a reset of the sociopolitical space. “We do not simply manufacture policies out of thin air. We listen to our people, hear what they want to see, and incorporate their expectations into our agenda,” Makinde said. The governor disclosed that the party had partnered with Skill Reset Nigeria to train one million young Nigerians in skills intended to improve their employment prospects. He also identified high interest rates and inadequate access to long-term financing as major obstacles to manufacturing, promising to create a business environment that would encourage entrepreneurship and sustainable job creation. Makinde urged Nigerians to reject religious and ethnic divisions, arguing that the country’s challenges affected everyone. “Our message to you today is this: Please reject all forms of division along religious or ethnic lines. The challenges we face do not discriminate on the basis of religion or ethnicity,” he said. The governor also criticised President Bola Tinubu’s planned trip to Saudi Arabia to pray for Nigeria, saying leaders should combine prayers with honesty and action at home. “Prayers can also be answered here in Nigeria. Please, we will remain here, pray for our country and pray for our leaders because Nigeria belongs to all of us,” Makinde said. He urged supporters to protect their Permanent Voter Cards and use them in the 2027 election, alleging that political opponents were distributing money to buy support and destroying the party’s campaign materials. “Let them pull down our posters. item.title: NAFDAC destroys N8bn fake, banned products in North-Central
item.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) has seized and destroyed fake, adulterated, expired and banned products worth more than ₦8 billion across North-Central Nigeria. The Director-General of NAFDAC, Prof. Mojisola Adeyeye, disclosed this on Thursday in Lafia, Nasarawa State, saying the products were confiscated from manufacturing facilities, sales outlets, markets and motor parks across the zone. Adeyeye, who was represented by a Deputy Director of the agency in the zone, Joseph Edor, said the bulk of the destroyed products comprised banned alcoholic beverages packaged in sachets and containers smaller than 200 millilitres. She explained that the restriction on alcoholic beverages in sachets and glass bottles below 200ml was introduced because their affordability, availability and portability made them susceptible to abuse, particularly among young people and underage schoolchildren. According to her, early exposure to alcohol can affect brain development and damage vital organs, including the liver and kidneys. “Research has shown that early exposure to alcohol affects the brain and other vital organs such as the liver and kidneys,” she said. She added that alcohol consumption among children could contribute to impaired brain development, poor academic performance, reduced productivity and other health complications. Adeyeye said NAFDAC was established under Decree No. 19 of 1993, as amended, with the responsibility of protecting public health by ensuring that regulated products manufactured, imported, distributed and sold in Nigeria meet the required quality and safety standards. She said the ban on certain alcoholic beverages and the subsequent enforcement operations were aimed at curbing abuse, addiction and associated health risks. Other items seized during the operations included expired and counterfeit medicines, as well as adulterated and unwholesome food products and cosmetics. The director-general commended law enforcement agencies, sister agencies and other stakeholders for supporting NAFDAC’s operations through intelligence sharing and the provision of security. The Nasarawa State Coordinator of NAFDAC, Dr. Gyani Stephen, said the exercise was intended to protect public health rather than harm traders or businesses. She warned dealers in counterfeit and banned products to desist from the practice, adding that the agency would take legal action against offenders. In a goodwill message, the Nasarawa State Commander of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency, Daniel Saidu, represented by Yakubu Awoh, commended NAFDAC for its efforts to protect lives through the seizure and destruction of expired and counterfeit products. item.title: Obi promises emergency measures on security, corruption, poverty
item.description: Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Mr Peter Obi, has promised emergency measures to tackle insecurity, corruption, hunger and poverty, if elected. Obi made the promise on Thursday during an interactive town hall meeting with a large crowd of supporters across party lines in Abakaliki. The former Anambra governor said that Nigeria required purposeful leadership to achieve sustainable development, adding that he possessed the character, experience and capacity to lead the country. He said that Nigeria had vast arable land and other resources that could transform its economy if properly harnessed. According to him, the country must shift from consumption to production, particularly through agriculture and other productive sectors. On the Federal Government’s borrowing, Obi said taking loans was not inherently wrong but became problematic when the funds were used for consumption rather than productive investments. “It becomes wrong when the government borrows to buy a yacht or a presidential plane for consumption purposes,” he said. He pledged that his administration would ensure transparency in public borrowing, insisting that Nigerians must know why loans were obtained and how the funds would be utilised. On security, the presidential candidate promised to deploy modern technology and other effective measures to tackle insecurity and guarantee the safety of citizens across the country, irrespective of their locations. Obi also vowed that anyone found guilty of corruption, including the president, would face prosecution and imprisonment in accordance with the law. He said his vision was to build a Nigeria where citizens could achieve their aspirations through merit rather than personal connections. “My dream is to see a Nigeria where the son of a nobody can become somebody without knowing anybody,” he added. Obi, who expressed excitement over the turnout at the meeting, described himself as the most credible among the three leading presidential candidates. He cited President Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress (APC), former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and himself as the leading contenders. He urged Nigerians to participate actively in the forthcoming election and protect their votes. “You should vote for me because I am the most credible candidate among the leading candidates for the presidency,” he said. Obi expressed optimism that Nigeria could achieve meaningful transformation under credible leadership, pledging to provide such leadership if elected. item.title: ‘Horrific’ Russian Drone Strike Kills 14 At Ukraine Train Station
item.description: A Russian drone slammed into a busy platform at a railway station in Ukraine’s Dnipro on Thursday killing at least 14 people in what President Volodymyr Zelensky called a “horrific” attack that demands a response from Kyiv’s allies. The strike came as Ukraine and Russia strive to uphold a fragile local ceasefire in the ravaged city of Oleshky — under Russian occupation since 2022 and where residents have faced months of food, water and medicine shortages. The truce was holding into its third day, both countries said, with the Ukrainian human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets announcing that he had “set out with the Ukrainian delegation towards Oleshky” through Belarus and Russia. But elsewhere, Moscow continued to pummel Ukraine. The strike at the Dnipro train station hit a platform “where a regular commuter train and a regular passenger train were standing”, Zelensky said. By early Thursday afternoon, Dnipropetrovsk regional governor Oleksandr Ganzha said the death toll from the strike had risen to 14.
